walkthroughs.body_html:
External Influences on Business Activity — a core area of GCSE Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

External Influences on Business Activity brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with External Influences on Business Activity.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why can a profitable business still fail?
options: Because cash flow and profit are different — a business may be profitable on paper but run out of cash to pay bills, especially if customers owe money or stock ties up funds.
If a business is profitable it cannot run out of money.
Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness only.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.

mcqs.q: Why are hygiene factors and motivators not on the same scale in Herzberg's theory?
options: Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness only.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Hygiene factors and motivators are just two types of motivation that combine.

Hygiene factors only prevent dissatisfaction (their absence demotivates, presence is neutral); motivators create satisfaction (their presence motivates, absence is neutral). They affect different outcomes, not different points on one scale.

mcqs.q: Why might a business adopt corporate social responsibility (CSR)?
options: CSR is the legal requirement to pay taxes.
Reasons include genuine ethics, but also commercial benefits — improved reputation, customer loyalty, employee retention, and reduced regulatory or reputational risk.
CSR is purely about being ethical with no business benefit.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
